text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 58 billion levs in the second half of March to 298 billion levs, preliminary Finance ministry figures showed.
The deficit at end-March was 1.43 percent of the nominal Gross Domestic Product for this year assumed in financial accord between the caretaker cabinet and the International Monetary Fund. @
-- Bulgaria's Interior Miniotry planned to launch a Mosquito-2 operation against tax evasion after April 15, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said.
Under the Mosquito-1 operation at the end of March police checked the origin of more than 14,000 luxury cars to beat car theft and tax evasion.
-- Bulgaria's Health ministry owes some $19 million to suppliers of medicines, the Association of foreign pharmaceutical producers in Bulgaria said.

-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines plans to stabilise its finances by buying out the foreign debt of some local banks placed in receivership and repay its debt to those banks at a discount, Balkan executive director Valeri Doganov said.

-- Bulgaria hopes to receive an extra balance of payments support from its European creditors in addition to funding agreed with G-24 and European Union countries, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to offer for sale its 23 percent stake in the Chimimport chemical trading company, Trade minister Daniela Bobeva said.
-- The Bulgarian State Railways (BSR) company is expected to raise passenger fares by 60 percent from April 20, BSR officials said.
-- The Sofia Municipal Privatisation Agency (SMPA) hopes to receive 5.1 billion levs in proceeds from 230 sell-offs planned for this year, SMPA executive director Ivan Dimitrov said.
-- The Institute for Weather Forecast at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences said air temperatures in Bulgaria in April have reached record lows for the past 104 years.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov is expected to meet today the leader of the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) Georgi Parvanov.

The meeting was scheduled following Parvanov's letter to the president, in which he said that BSP had withdrawn its support for the interim government and was likely to withdraw from the Consultative Council for National Security. @
